title: IELTS Reading: Skimming and Scanning to Beat the Clock
summary: Two reading gears — skim for gist, scan for answers — plus how to survive 40 questions in 60 minutes with no extra transfer time.

nodes.note: Gist + structure of each passage in ~2 minutes

nodes.note: Know what you're hunting before you dive back in

chunks.heading: Skim vs scan — two different gears
chunks.body: **Skimming** is reading fast for the **general idea** — titles, first lines, topic sentences. **Scanning** is hunting for **specific information** like a name, date or keyword. You use skim to map the passage, then scan to land each answer.
chunks.realExample: Skim a paragraph and you learn 'this one is about how bees navigate.' Scan the same paragraph for '1962' and your eyes jump straight to the date without reading every word.
chunks.memoryHook: Skim = the map. Scan = the search. Map first, search second.

chunks.heading: Read the questions, then hunt
chunks.body: After a quick skim, **read the questions before re-reading the text**. Underline the keyword in each question so you know exactly what to scan for. Most question sets follow the **order of the passage**, so answers appear roughly top to bottom.
chunks.realExample: Question: 'Which decade saw the sharpest decline?' Keyword = 'decade / decline'. You now scan only for dates and downward language, ignoring everything else.
chunks.memoryHook: Never read the passage twice blind. Questions first, then targeted hunting.

chunks.heading: Answers are paraphrased — match meaning, not words
chunks.body: The text rarely uses the **same words** as the question; it uses **synonyms**. Train yourself to match **meaning**. The word you scan for in your head may be a paraphrase of what's printed.
chunks.realExample: Question says 'children'; the passage says 'youngsters'. Question says 'expensive'; passage says 'costly'. Same idea, different word — that swap is often the whole test.
chunks.memoryHook: IELTS hides answers behind synonyms. Hunt the idea, not the exact word.

chunks.heading: Mind the clock — and there's no transfer time
chunks.body: You have **60 minutes for 40 questions across 3 passages** — about **20 minutes each**. Unlike Listening, Reading gives you **no extra time** to copy answers, so **write them straight onto the answer sheet** as you go and don't leave blanks.
chunks.realExample: Stuck on one question at minute 18 of a passage? Guess, mark it, and move on — an unanswered question and a wrong guess score the same, but the guess might be right.
chunks.memoryHook: 20-20-20 and write as you go. No blanks, no transfer time.

recall.q: What's the difference between skimming and scanning?
recall.a: Skimming is fast reading for the general idea; scanning is hunting for specific information like a keyword, name or date.

recall.q: How long is the IELTS Reading test and how many questions?
recall.a: 60 minutes for 40 questions, across 3 passages — roughly 20 minutes per passage.

recall.q: Does Reading give you extra time to transfer your answers?
recall.a: No — unlike Listening, there is no extra transfer time, so write answers straight onto the answer sheet.

recall.q: Why should you read the questions before re-reading the passage?
recall.a: So you know the keyword to scan for; and because answers usually follow the order of the passage.

recall.q: Why won't the passage use the same words as the question?
recall.a: IELTS paraphrases — answers are hidden behind synonyms, so you must match meaning, not the exact word.
